kemz.seoTitle: KEMZ equipment catalog website — design, CMS and SEO
kemz.seoDescription: KEMZ factory website case: redesign, equipment catalog with model pages, technical inquiries, CMS and SEO. The mobile PageSpeed Insights score reached 95.
kemz.lead: A new factory website: from an urgent brief and design concept to the equipment catalog, CMS, forms, and launch.
kemz.title: Making complex manufacturing clear
kemz.intro: I urgently rebuilt the factory website as a B2B sales tool: bold industrial design, an equipment catalog, technical inquiries, a CMS, and SEO — from concept to launch.
kemz.caption: Actual screen of the updated KEMZ website
kemz.archiveTitle: Strong manufacturing. A weak digital front door.
kemz.archiveIntro: The former site had a side menu, rotating product banner, and long factory introduction. Engineers and buyers had to search for the right machine, its specifications, and a way to make a technical inquiry. I rebuilt the structure around those tasks.
kemz.archiveBeforeText: Scattered navigation and a generic template buried the essentials: specific equipment and the customer's next step.
kemz.archiveAfterAlt: Updated KEMZ home page with a catalog link and key company data
kemz.archiveAfterText: Large typography, real machinery, and signature blue. The first screen leads to the catalog, documents, and an inquiry with project parameters.
kemz.contextTitle: The site slowed the journey from equipment model to inquiry
kemz.contextText: According to the KEMZ team, the former site loaded slowly, converted too few relevant visitors, and gave product pages little search visibility. Forms let spam through, while some important inquiries failed to reach sales. This needed a fast, complete rebuild of the customer journey, not a cosmetic update.
kemz.scopeTitle: From a factory problem to a working sales tool
kemz.scope1Text: I removed the old template's visual noise. Oversized type, quarry textures, signature blue, and real machinery convey the scale of production without obscuring technical details.
kemz.scope2Text: I built a route from product category to model, with specifications, documents, and clear navigation. The CMS lets the team update products and news on its own.
kemz.scope3Text: I created a technical inquiry with equipment parameters, field validation, and spam protection, then routed requests to the right team.
kemz.scope4Text: I optimized loading, mobile experience, and Core Web Vitals, then prepared product-page structure, metadata, and a sitemap for search engines.
kemz.screenTitle: From the opening screen to an actual inquiry
kemz.screenText: Visitors can immediately see what the factory makes. The next step is a catalog organized by application, followed by an inquiry form with technical parameters.
kemz.proofTitle: Faster. Clearer. Closer to an inquiry.
kemz.proofNote: The website is faster, while content and inquiries are easier for the team to manage.
kemz.reviewDraftText: “Thank you for the fast turnaround. The new site helps us present our equipment and receive more precise customer inquiries.”
contextItems: A confusing route to a model
kemz.solutionIntro: Design concept, development, content, and deployment in one fast delivery.
kemz.detailsText: Engineers and buyers can start with a product category, inspect a model's specifications, and send the factory the requirements of their project. These are fragments of that interface.
kemz.journeyCatalogText: Search, categories, and filters narrow the list to relevant models.
kemz.journeyProductText: A product page brings together the description, technical data, and an inquiry action.
kemz.journeyRequestText: The form carries equipment type, machine model, and required power.
kemz.insideIntro: I planned not only the public pages, but also how the team updates the catalog, receives inquiries, and grows search visibility.
kemz.insideCmsText: The CMS stores categories, models, descriptions, images, and news. The team can keep product information current.
kemz.insideLeadsText: The technical form collects selection details and contacts. Field validation and spam protection help keep valuable inquiries visible.
kemz.insideSeoText: Categories and models have their own URLs, titles, and descriptions; the site also provides a sitemap, canonicals, and structured data.
kemz.resultText: The site is faster, and the route to equipment and technical inquiries is shorter. The mobile PageSpeed Insights score rose from roughly 60–70 to 95. Accessibility and SEO each scored 100.
kemz.outcomeTitle: One partner, the full project journey
kemz.outcomeText: The site brings together the company story, catalog, news, documents, and technical inquiries. Design, development, content, and launch preparation form one process.
kemz.discuss: Need a site with this level of depth?

VneCase.deliveryTitle: From illustration to working landing page
VneCase.deliveryLead: I built the responsive static page with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and published it at vneshablona.ru. The illustrations support the story; the form and search files work as part of the site.
VneCase.insideTitle: A lightweight page with a working form
VneCase.insideText: The landing page is hosted as static files. To send an inquiry, it calls an API at jakuninoleg.dev, where the submission is checked and delivered by email. The page needs no separate server.

About.title: From the idea and design to code and launch
About.lead: I treat a website as one complete product: understand the brief and audience, design the interface, build it, and prepare it for use and search.
About.name: Oleg Jakunin
About.profileText: I have worked in web development since 2017. I studied full-stack development at Le Wagon Barcelona and later mentored its students. At major fintech companies, I built ERP systems, financial dashboards, and tools with complex business logic. I also worked in an international team on products for overseas clients. Since 2022, I have led website and web-product projects independently, from the initial brief through launch.
